correctness.rationale: For each feasible reversible kernel, the bipartition contrast vector gives Rayleigh quotient 1-T/(ab), while the q-1 dimensional larger-part zero-sum subspace gives mean quotient 1-T/b. Uniform edge flow attains the two lower bounds via the exactly factored spectrum. Scalar minimax gives unique T* including a=1/3 boundary. Equality at the upper spectral bound forces all larger-class zero-sum vectors to be actual eigenvectors, hence edge-flow rows constant; at T=a capacities force all row totals equal, and at T<a the negative-extreme cut-vector equation forces the same. Thus no asymmetric optimizer exists. Exact rational symbolic tests 112, 1,800 random feasible comparisons, 45 zero-sum perturbations, eight MH checks and six numerical optimizations passed; numerical checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Provides a closed-form solution to a standard nonuniform reversible Markov sampling design problem, a sharp 1/3 criterion for optimality of the widely used Metropolis rule, and rigidity of the optimizer under independently adjustable transitions for every bipartition size p,q>=2. The hard part is proving uniqueness beyond symmetry reduction, not reparametrizing an already-known symmetric spectrum.
